channel.title: AffineDrift
channel.description: Affine control theory for golf swing dynamics - Research articles, models, and resources

item.title: Affine Control Interpretation of the Golf Swing — Part 4
item.description: Modal approximations, wrench decomposition, and pendulum dynamics with detailed mathematical derivations for golf swing biomechanics.

item.title: Affine Control Interpretation of the Golf Swing — Part 2
item.description: Diagnostic tools for analyzing golf swing dynamics: the Zero Torque Counterfactual (ZTCF) and Zero Velocity Counterfactual (ZVCF) for separating passive and active forces.

item.title: Rotation Representation Converter
item.description: Interactive calculator for converting between rotation matrices, quaternions, ZYX Euler angles, axis-angle, and exponential coordinates — with 3D screw axis visualization and step-by-step formulas.

item.title: Passive Distributed Control: Frans Bosch Framework
item.description: Integration of Frans Bosch's passive distributed control framework with the Geometry of Motion mathematical treatment.

item.title: Ideomotor Theory and the Predictive Brain Model
item.description: Cross-cutting treatment of ideomotor theory, predictive coding, and forward models as they relate to motor control and the Geometry of Motion framework.

item.title: The Drifter Manifesto
item.description: The foundational theory series establishing the control-affine framework for golf swing analysis, including drift/input decomposition, ZTCF, ZVCF, drift invariance, and numerical implementation.

item.title: Degrees of Freedom and the Curse of Dimensionality
item.description: A cross-cutting treatment of the degrees-of-freedom problem and curse of dimensionality as it appears throughout the Geometry of Motion series.

item.title: Zero-Torque Counterfactual
item.description: The Zero-Torque Counterfactual (ZTCF): definition, interpretation, and numerical computation algorithm for the AffineDrift golf swing framework.

item.title: Affine Control Interpretation of the Golf Swing — Part 5
item.description: Simulink implementation documentation for the control-affine golf swing model, including numerical routines and validation approaches.

item.title: Affine Control Interpretation of the Golf Swing — Part 3
item.description: Establishes drift invariance properties and develops a taxonomy of forces in the golf swing, analyzing the limitations of the affine control assumption.

item.title: Affine Control Interpretation of the Golf Swing
item.description: Foundational derivation showing the golf swing as a control-affine mechanical system, introducing the drift/input decomposition framework for biomechanical analysis.

item.title: A Control-Theoretic, Multibody Dynamics, and Relativistic-Analogy Analysis of the Drift–Control Ratio in the Golf Swing
item.description: Analysis of the drift-to-control ratio in golf swings using control theory, multibody dynamics, and relativistic analogies to understand passive dynamics exploitation.

item.title: Rotation Representations: A Cross-Reference Guide
item.description: Comprehensive reference for conversion between rotation matrices, quaternions, Euler angles, and screw/axis-angle representations.

item.title: UpstreamDrift: Educational Tool Integration Guide
item.description: Review of UpstreamDrift simulation platform capabilities and integration plan for the Geometry of Motion book series.

item.title: Classic Sources of Nonlinearity in Mechanical Systems: A Comprehensive Review for the Control-Affine Framework
item.description: A comprehensive catalog of nonlinearity sources in mechanical and biomechanical systems, examining how each interacts with the control-affine framework and force superposition.

item.title: Constraint Torques at the Wrist: How Grip Angle Influences Force Transmission and Face Angle Variability in the Golf Swing
item.description: Biomechanical model of the left wrist as a universal joint, analyzing how grip angle influences force transmission and clubface angle variability.

item.title: Superposition in Affine Control Systems via Newton–Euler, Lagrangian, and Screw-Theoretic Formulations
item.description: Rigorous derivation of input superposition in affine control systems using Newton-Euler, Lagrangian, and screw-theoretic formulations with applications to biomechanics.

item.title: On the Limits of Strokes-Gained Inference for Individual Golfers
item.description: Statistical and methodological limitations of strokes gained analysis for individual golfer assessment, with recommendations for proper interpretation.

item.title: Secondary Axis Stability in Golf Clubs: Mechanical Foundations and Implications for Putter Design
item.description: Mechanical analysis of secondary axis rotation stability in golf clubs, with implications for putter design and face angle consistency.

item.title: Screw Theory Reference for Control-Affine Multibody Dynamics
item.description: Reference guide for screw theory notation and concepts in control-affine multibody dynamics, including twists, wrenches, and exponential coordinates.

item.title: The Null Space of the Constraint Jacobian: Unconstrained Motion in Constrained Systems with Applications to Golf Swing Biomechanics
item.description: Analysis of unconstrained motion within constrained biomechanical systems using null space projections, applied to golf swing joint coordination.

item.title: Nonlinear Control Theory Insights, Drift Causality, and Future Research Directions
item.description: Insights from nonlinear control theory on drift causality in golf biomechanics, with future research directions for the control-affine framework.

item.title: Lagrangian Reference for Control-Affine Multibody Dynamics
item.description: Reference guide for Lagrangian mechanics applied to control-affine multibody systems, bridging classical mechanics and modern control theory.

item.title: Interpretation of Inverse Dynamics: Understanding the Fundamental Limitations
item.description: Critical examination of inverse dynamics limitations in biomechanics, explaining why calculated torques don't represent actual muscle contributions.

item.title: Section Y: Inference from Inverse Dynamics in a Nonlinear Affine System
item.description: Inference challenges in applying inverse dynamics to nonlinear affine systems, with implications for golf swing biomechanical analysis.

item.title: Intentional Constraint Collapse at Impact: How Golfers Generate High Force with Stable Club Motion
item.description: Analysis of how golfers generate high impact forces while maintaining stable club motion through intentional constraint release at ball contact.

item.title: Force and Mobility Ellipsoids in the Golf Swing: A Geometric Interpretation Using the Double Pendulum
item.description: Force and mobility ellipsoid analysis for the golf swing, providing geometric insights into directional strength and movement capabilities.

item.title: Natural vs Active Forces and Torques in Affine Mechanical Systems
item.description: Decomposition of natural versus active forces and torques in affine mechanical systems, with applications to double pendulum golf swing models.

item.title: Applications of the Control-Affine Framework in Golf Swing Biomechanics
item.description: Practical applications of the control-affine decomposition framework in golf swing analysis, training, and equipment design.

item.title: Affine Control Interpretation of the Golf Swing: Drift, Input, and Causal Decomposition of Forces - Part I: Theoretical Foundations
item.description: Comprehensive theoretical foundation establishing the golf swing as a control-affine system, with detailed analysis of drift dynamics, input superposition, and causal force decomposition.
